newsitem.title: ITALY: Lakeside villa was hideaway for glamorous Versace.
newsitem.headline: Lakeside villa was hideaway for glamorous Versace.

text.p: When glamorous supermodel Naomi Campbell needed to get away from it all last month after a blazing row with her boyfriend, she took refuge in the lakeside villa that was Gianni Versace's hideaway.

Other stars of the international jet-set, including pop and movie icons Madonna, Silvester Stallone and Bruce Springsteen, have all been guests of the murdered Italian fashion king at his Villa Fontanelle on the shores of Lake Como.
But for the villagers of Moltrasio, Versace was a remote figure with a glittering lifestyle they could only dream of.
Locals remember him as a tycoon who would fly in by helicopter to a nearby hotel before being whisked by motor launch to his aristocratic 18th century villa.
He hardly ever ventured into the small village.
"I've lived here all my life and I never saw him even once," said Carlo Donegani, 81.
Locals said the 50-year-old fashion designer, who was shot dead on Tuersday on the steps of his Spanish-style mansion in Miami Beach, had been coming to the villa for a decade.
The designer's sister Donatella and brother Santo brought his ashes home on Friday and laid them to rest in the village's secluded cemetery.

Despite the glamorous company Versace kept and his jet-set lifestyle as king of raunchy glamour with royalty and rockstars clamouring for his clothes, the designer and his close-knit family appeared to revel in the beautiful, tranquil location.
Donatella was married at the local church and her two children, Allegra and Daniel, were baptised there.
"I only saw him a few times, when I used to go to baptise the family at the home at Easter time," said village priest Bartolomeo Franzi. "For us it was something to boast about to have them here."
Laura, who works in a restaurant in Moltrasio said she was pleased he had chosen to be laid to rest there. "At least they said when he died that he wanted to be buried here," she said.
"That was probably the first time anybody had ever heard of this place."

Residents said they occasionally caught glimpses of Versace and his famous guests at the three-storey yellow lakeside villa set back from the road and shielded by a cluster of tall trees, or when Versace sailed his boat on the lake.

Campbell, a favourite model and close friend of the Versace family, sought refuge at Villa Fontanelle after reports that she had taken an overdose after a spectacular row with her lover, the fiery flamenco star Joaquin Cortes.
"He came here to get away from it all when he needed a rest," said village resident Sergio Annoni. "He didn't come here to have a drink with the locals at the bar."
Versace, originally from Reggio Calabria in Italy's poor south, sped along fashion's fast lane and felt at home in Milan, Paris, London, New York and Paris.
"The only way you could tell he was in residence at Villa Fontanelle was when there were security guards at the gate," said Laura, who declined to give her second name.
That security cordon contrasted starkly with Versace's free-wheeling existence in Miami.
He was shot dead at point-blank range by a lone gunman as he walked home alone in broad daylight from buying magazines.
Moltrasio looked kindly on its famous neighbour. "What we appreciate is that he chose to have a home here because this place is simply so beautiful," Annoni said.
But just like his sumptuous lifestyle, the crime thriller manner of Versace's death was totally alien to his neighbours.
"In my opinion people thought, 'well these are just things that can happen to you when you live in that kind of world'," Laura said.
